{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mi-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"659d353e30e0ed7db3d30d9c003af29a59a36fdc1e0e0c2fedccb036523299dd","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mi-class-std:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"7af7437894a2c63b20529c8a1ed7c10696796036051dd6666178ab579008ca37","source_liveness_sha256":"e81e5179580dc89fb25fdf5194e9f75291db3aa019fc21ccfe32c38d1a9df42f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Residency, licenses and REAL ID","heading":"C — Residency, licenses and REAL ID","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Residency, licenses and REAL ID

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
To count as a Michigan resident, you have to live in Michigan and have shown that you are legally present in the state. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
State law bars the Secretary of State from issuing an original driver’s license or state ID card to anyone who is not a legal Michigan resident. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
A new resident must title and register their vehicle at a Secretary of State office right away, handing in the title or ownership proof from the former home state. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
A driver’s license or state ID from another state may be used until your Michigan residency is established, and after that you apply for the Michigan card at a Secretary of State office. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
Michigan requests your driving record from your former home state, and that record becomes part of your Michigan driving record. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
If your out-of-state license is suspended or revoked, you must settle the open issues with that former state before Michigan will accept your license application. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
Once your Michigan application is accepted, the out-of-state license is invalidated and handed back, because Michigan lets a driver hold only one valid license at a time. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
Licensing requirements differ by license type, group designator and endorsement, and specialized licenses such as a chauffeur’s license or a commercial driver’s license may add testing and a background check. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
Someone who has never held a license from any state or country is refused a Michigan license when their record shows two or more moving-violation convictions within three years of the application date. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
To apply for a license, your driving record may carry no more than one conviction within the three years before you apply. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
The operator’s license is Michigan’s basic driver’s license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
A chauffeur’s license needs a minimum age of 16 and a passed written chauffeur’s test, and it is required when your job is mainly driving a vehicle rated 10,000 pounds GVWR or more, carrying passengers or property for hire, or driving a bus or school bus. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
A commercial driver’s license is required for a single vehicle rated 26,001 pounds GVWR or more, a combination towing 10,001 pounds or more when the GCWR is 26,001 pounds or more, a vehicle built to carry 16 or more people counting the driver, or placarded hazardous materials. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
Commercial drivers must be at least 18 and suspension-free for the 36 months before applying; drivers aged 18 to 21 may drive commercially only inside Michigan, and age 21 is needed to cross state lines or haul placarded hazardous materials. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
An enhanced driver’s license lets you come back into the United States from Canada, Mexico, Bermuda and the Caribbean, by land or by sea, with no other identity papers, and enhanced cards are also REAL ID compliant. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
Graduated licenses, namely the Level 1 Learner’s, Level 2 Intermediate and Level 3 Full, are issued through Michigan’s driver education program for teens under 18. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
A valid operator’s or chauffeur’s license already covers riding a moped, but a suspended, revoked or denied license makes you ineligible for a moped license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
An unlicensed teen age 15 or older with a parent’s approval may apply for a moped license and must take vision, written knowledge and traffic sign tests. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
A CY motorcycle endorsement requires either a rider education course or the written knowledge test plus a motorcycle skills test, and the course is mandatory for riders aged 16 to 17 and for adults who fail the skills test twice. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
A CY 3W restriction limits a rider to three-wheeled motorcycles and is earned through a three-wheeled safety course or the written test plus a three-wheel skills test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
The recreational double R endorsement, which requires a knowledge test, covers a pickup pulling a fifth-wheel recreational trailer with a second trailer hitched behind it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A02
The farmer endorsement lets farm operations move equipment, livestock and produce, and it may call for a general knowledge test and a combination vehicles test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A02
Starting May 7, 2025, Michigan residents need a REAL ID-compliant document to board a domestic flight or to enter certain federal facilities, military bases and nuclear power plants. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A03
REAL ID-compliant documents include licenses and IDs from states meeting the federal standard and valid U.S. passports and passport cards, and the TSA lists acceptable documents at tsa.gov. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A03
A Michigan card is REAL ID compliant when its upper right corner shows a star in a gold circle or a star inside a Michigan outline, and enhanced cards without a star still comply and receive the star at renewal or replacement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A03
REAL ID is optional, and you may not need it if you neither fly nor plan to enter those federal sites, or if you hold an acceptable alternative such as a valid U.S. passport. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A03
Adding REAL ID costs nothing extra when you renew, but applying for it at any other time means paying the duplicate card fee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A03
A standard card without REAL ID is marked “Not for Federal Identification” yet still works for driving and as identification for cashing checks, renting vehicles, buying age-restricted items and entering casinos. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A03
Newcomers from another state or country should apply for a Michigan license once residency is established, bringing proof of a Social Security number, of U.S. citizenship or legal presence, of identity and of Michigan residency. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A03
After your documents are approved a vision test is given, and a newcomer may also need the written knowledge test, a temporary instruction permit (TIP) and a driving skills test. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A03
A license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany or the Republic of Korea can be converted to a Michigan license without the knowledge test, TIP or skills test. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A03
Holding an expired foreign license, or an out-of-state license expired for at least four years, means you must get a TIP and pass a driving skills test before Michigan issues a license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A03
Your photo is taken and a fee set by license type and add-ons is charged, and the new Michigan license should arrive by mail in about three weeks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A03
Applicants under 18 must complete Graduated Driver Licensing, a step waived for anyone who has held a valid license from another state for more than a year. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0017]
